Question: Each of \(6\) balls is randomly and independently painted either black or white with equal probability. What is the probability that every ball is different in color from more than half of the other \(5\) balls?
Solution:
Each ball needs more than half of the other five balls to have the opposite color. That means it needs at least three opposite-color balls.

If either color occurs four or more times, a ball of that color sees at most two of the other color and fails the condition. Thus the condition holds exactly when there are three balls of each color. There are \(\binom63=20\) such assignments out of \(2^6=64\) equally likely color assignments, giving
\[
\frac{20}{64}=\boxed{\frac5{16}},
\]
choice D.
